description: Construction number 4831. Ferried to São Tomé on 30 July 1969 with CanRelief Air for the Biafran airlift and never left; with its sister CF-NAM it is the last physical remnant of the Biafra relief bridge. Retained beside the airport road and fitted out commercially, one airframe as a restaurant and the other as a discotheque. Currency is the weak point: the last first-hand account found is a Friends of São Tomé and Príncipe campaign report of 15 January 2020 describing both as standing but deteriorating and seeking monument status; OpenStreetMap carries a live restaurant node named The Airplane 25 m from the recorded position; but Esri WorldView-3 imagery of 17 September 2023 at this spot resolves only two long white fuselage-shaped objects among trees and buildings, with no wings distinguishable, and no complete four-engined airframe is visible anywhere else around the airport. Recorded as still present on the balance of that evidence, flagged as needing a ground check.

Construction number 4832, the second of the pair ferried to São Tomé on 30 July 1969 for the Biafran airlift and left in place. Sources do not consistently say which of CF-NAL and CF-NAM became the restaurant and which the discotheque, so the fit-out is not attributed to either airframe individually. Same currency caveat as its sister: last confirmed standing by the January 2020 preservation campaign report, not unambiguously resolvable in the September 2023 satellite imagery.
